failure_summary.description: Follow-up constraints triggered fresh searches instead of retrieving and filtering applicable cached results.
Search or filter outputs were not consistently assigned and saved as required.
A hotel search was called without mandatory check-in and checkout dates rather than seeking the missing details.
Flight times were converted to a 24-hour seconds format rejected by the tool.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers cache retrieval, filtering, and saving, so repeating those rules would not patch a content gap. The actionable gaps are the conflict between generic time examples and the accepted flight-time format, and ambiguity about proceeding with complete domains when another requested domain lacks mandatory inputs.

edits.content: - For flight time ranges, use the accepted 12-hour AM/PM format (for example, `08:23 PM`); do not convert to 24-hour or seconds strings, even if generic tool examples show them. Represent an exact time as `[time, time]`; represent “arrive by time” as `["12:00 AM", time]`.

edits.target: Before calling a travel tool, check its required parameters against the full conversation and available context. If any required details are missing, use `seek_information` to ask only for those details; do not invent values, pass `None`, or run a partial search. For requests spanning multiple domains, bundle missing required details for all requested domains into the same information request. Do not ask for optional preferences.
edits.content: Before any call, validate mandatory inputs separately for each requested tool or domain and each flight leg. If a requested tool lacks a mandatory input, do not call it or run a partial search; ask for only the missing mandatory details in one `seek_information` request across all incomplete domains or legs. Continue with every other requested domain whose mandatory inputs are complete, assigning and caching its result. Never invent values, pass `None`, or ask for optional preferences.
